title: Design Authentication Manager
statement:
Build a class `AuthenticationManager` that keeps track of login tokens. Every token stays valid for `timeToLive` seconds counted from the last moment it was created or renewed.

- `AuthenticationManager(timeToLive)` starts with no tokens and remembers the lifetime `timeToLive`.
- `generate(tokenId, currentTime)` creates a token named `tokenId` at second `currentTime`; it expires at second `currentTime + timeToLive`.
- `renew(tokenId, currentTime)`: if a token named `tokenId` exists and has not expired by `currentTime`, its expiry moves to `currentTime + timeToLive`. If there is no such unexpired token, the call has no effect.
- `countUnexpiredTokens(currentTime)` returns how many tokens have not expired by `currentTime`.

A token whose expiry time equals the time of a call is already expired for that call: expiry is applied first. The `currentTime` values strictly increase from one call to the next, and `generate` never receives the same `tokenId` twice.
constraints: tokenId contains only lowercase English letters
Every call to generate uses a different tokenId
currentTime strictly increases across all calls
At most 2000 calls are made in total
notes:
## Intuition

The simple solution keeps a map from token to expiry time and scans all of it on every count, which is O(n) per count. A neater observation removes the scan: `timeToLive` never changes and `currentTime` only grows, so every expiry written (by `generate` or `renew`) is later than every expiry already stored. If tokens are kept in the order their expiry was last set, that order is also the order in which they expire, and the expired ones always sit at the front. A JavaScript `Map` remembers insertion order, so it can play the role of a hash map plus a linked list.

## Approach

1. Store `timeToLive` and an empty `expiries` map (token → expiry time).
2. `generate` appends the token with expiry `currentTime + timeToLive`.
3. `removeExpired(currentTime)` walks the map from the front, deleting entries whose `expiry` is at most `currentTime`, and stops at the first live one.
4. `renew` first removes expired tokens. If `tokenId` is no longer in the map, it does nothing. Otherwise it deletes the token and inserts it again, so it moves to the back with its new expiry.
5. `countUnexpiredTokens` removes expired tokens and returns the map's size.

## Example 1, step by step

With `timeToLive = 5`: `renew("aaa", 1)` finds nothing. `generate("aaa", 2)` stores `aaa → 7`. `countUnexpiredTokens(6)`: `7 > 6`, so nothing is removed and the answer is `1`. `generate("bbb", 7)` stores `bbb → 12`. `renew("aaa", 8)` first removes `aaa` (`7 <= 8`) and stops at `bbb`; `aaa` is gone, so nothing changes. `renew("bbb", 10)` moves `bbb` to expiry `15`. `countUnexpiredTokens(15)` removes `bbb` (`15 <= 15`) and returns `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1) amortised per call: each stored expiry is deleted at most once, so all removals together cost no more than the calls that wrote them.
- Space: O(k) for the k tokens that are still in the map.

## Pitfalls

- Expiry wins ties: a token with expiry `t` is dead at time `t`, so test `expiry > currentTime` for "alive".
- Renewing an expired token must not bring it back; check that it is still alive before updating.
- `Map.set` on an existing key keeps its old position; delete it first so the order stays sorted by expiry.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `timeToLive` | how many seconds a token lives after it is created or renewed |
| `expiries` | map from token id to expiry time, ordered by expiry |
| `tokenId`, `currentTime` | the call's arguments |
| `expiry` | the expiry time of the entry being inspected in `removeExpired` |

narration.3: Remember how long every token lives.
narration.4: The map holds token ids with their expiry times, and its insertion order matches expiry order.
narration.8: A new token expires timeToLive seconds from now and joins the back of the map.
narration.12: Drop every token that has already expired at this moment, so expiry is applied before the renewal.
narration.13: Is the token missing, either never generated or just removed as expired?
narration.16: Take the token out so it can be re-inserted at the back.
narration.17: Insert it again with its new, latest expiry time.
narration.21: Clear out tokens that have expired by now.
narration.22: Everything left in the map is unexpired.
narration.26: Walk the tokens from the earliest expiry onwards.
narration.27: The first token still alive means every later one is alive too.
narration.30: This token expired at or before currentTime; delete it.
